children: 3,200 MW Chapar plant will be commissioned in phases from December 2030

Adani Power on Sunday laid the foundation stone for its 3,200 MW ultra-supercritical thermal power plant at Chapar in Assam’s Dhubri district, marking the start of a Rs 48,000-crore project. The plant is scheduled to be commissioned in phases from December 2030.

The Chapar project forms part of Adani Group’s planned Rs 63,000-crore investment in Assam’s power sector. The investment also includes two pumped storage projects with a combined capacity of 2,700 MW through Adani Green Energy, while the group’s investments across power, aviation and cement in the state are expected to exceed Rs 80,000 crore.

The Chapar plant will comprise four units of 800 MW each and use ultra-supercritical technology, along with high-efficiency systems and modern environmental safeguards, according to Adani Power. Once commissioned, the plant is expected to meet the power requirements of households, commercial establishments and industries in Assam.

The project is expected to generate up to 20,000 jobs during the construction phase and around 5,000 jobs once operational. Adani Power also said the plant would create opportunities for local contractors, suppliers, transport operators and service providers as part of its expanding vendor ecosystem in the state.

The group's Rs 63,000-crore power investment in Assam comprises around Rs 48,000 crore for the Chapar thermal power plant and approximately Rs 15,000 crore for two pumped storage plants with a combined capacity of 2,700 MW through Adani Green Energy.

Adani Energy Solutions is also implementing smart metering projects in Assam as part of efforts to modernise the state's power distribution infrastructure. The group has separately committed investments in the aviation and cement sectors in the state.

Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said the Chapar project was among the largest single investments made in the state and would contribute to economic activity and SGST revenues. He also said local industries and enterprises would have opportunities to participate in the emerging ecosystem.

Jeet Adani, director, Adani Group, said the project would provide electricity for homes, businesses and industries while creating jobs and opportunities for local contractors, suppliers and businesses. He said the Chapar plant would become the largest power generation asset in the Northeast once operational.

The Chapar plant is scheduled to be commissioned in phases from December 2030. The project is part of the group's wider investments in Assam, where Adani has said investments across power, aviation and cement will exceed Rs 80,000 crore.
